title: Bounded constructibility detected by open and exceptional closed restriction
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], one has
$$K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j^*K\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\ \text{and}\ i^!K\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$$
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Here $i^!:D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\to D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ is the bounded-below right adjoint of $i_*=Ri_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.2, using Expose XIII, Theorem 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 for open direct-image finiteness

proof.text: For either immersion $h=j,i$, inverse image on constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Applying [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] degreewise gives $\mathcal H^q(h^*L)=h^*\mathcal H^q(L)$. The constructibility assertion of [prop-constructible-pullback] applies to each cohomology sheaf. Thus both $j^*$ and $i^*$ preserve bounded constructibility and preserve any cohomological interval. This uses ordinary small-etale inverse image throughout.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), constant-ring specialization; etale-cohomology.tex, constructible pullback (lemma-pullback-constructible); homology.tex Tag 010N

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Hence its direct image on abelian sheaves is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. Direct image of constant-ring module sheaves has the same underlying abelian direct image, and the forgetful functor is faithful and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; it therefore detects vanishing of homology and exactness. Consequently $i_*$ on $\Lambda$-module sheaves is exact as well. The counit $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ of [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful] is $\Lambda$-linear, since its maps preserve addition and hence multiplication by every integer modulo $\ell^n$. Exactness allows both functors and this counit to be applied termwise to complexes. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], $\mathcal H^q(i_*L)=i_*\mathcal H^q(L)$; the same counit gives $i^*i_*L\cong L$ in the derived category. In particular $i_*$ preserves and reflects a cohomological interval.

For a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf $G$ on $Z$, its stalks are finite by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] identifies this finite-stratification notion with the source-library notion in the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-finite-stalk-module]. That node applies to the finite morphism $i$ and the Noetherian target $X$; it says that $i_*G$ is constructible. Use the same comparison to return to the finite-stratification notion. Applying this to every $\mathcal H^q(L)$ and using Step 2 shows that $i_*$ preserves bounded constructibility. Conversely, if $i_*L$ is bounded constructible, Step 1 and the termwise counit of Step 2 give $L\cong i^*i_*L$ bounded constructible. Thus closed direct image both preserves and reflects the property needed below.

source.place: Tag 095R (lemma-finite-pushforward-constructible), finite closed immersion into the Noetherian scheme X; Tags 095E, 03RU, 09XZ for the constructibility comparison

proof.text: First let $Q$ be a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U$ annihilated by $\ell$. Its same finite local constant module values are $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces, so it is constructible with $\mathbf F_\ell$ coefficients too. Excellence implies quasi-excellence by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Apply [lem-per-gabber-open-immersion-sheaf-finiteness] with $T=X$ and $B=\mathbf F_\ell$: each $R^qj_*Q$ computed over $B$ is constructible and is zero for $q$ sufficiently large, with a bound allowed to depend on $Q$. Apply [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] once with coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and once with $B$. Both resulting underlying abelian sheaves are $\mathcal H^q(Rj_*Q_{ab})$, so the higher direct images computed in the two module categories have isomorphic underlying abelian sheaves. This is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules: every group homomorphism commutes with the integer scalar actions, and the $\Lambda$ action here is multiplication modulo $\ell^n$. Thus the same finite local constant trivializations and the same vanishing bound apply over $\Lambda$. Negative higher direct images vanish for a sheaf in degree zero by the bounded-below derived construction [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Consequently $Rj_*(Q[0])$ is bounded constructible over $\Lambda$.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 1.1.1, prime-coefficient case; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree) for the two coefficient-forgetting comparisons

proof.text: For an arbitrary constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ on $U$, put $F_r=\operatorname{im}(\ell^r:F\to F)$ for $0\le r\le n$ and $Q_r=F_r/F_{r+1}$ for $0\le r<n$. By [thm-constructible-serre], $F_r$ is constructible (an image is the kernel of a cokernel) and so is $Q_r$. We have $F_n=0$, $F_0=F$, and $\ell Q_r=0$. Each short exact sequence $0\to F_{r+1}\to F_r\to Q_r\to0$, placed in degree zero, gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Apply the triangulated functor $Rj_*$ [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Step 4 supplies bounded constructibility of $Rj_*Q_r$; starting with $Rj_*F_n=0$ and descending from $r=n-1$ to $0$, the triangulated-subcategory assertion [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] supplies bounded constructibility of $Rj_*F_r$ at each stage. This proves the required open-direct-image assertion for every constructible sheaf over $\Lambda$ without assuming a bound uniform in all sheaves.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 1.1.1 and paragraph 1.1.2; the finite coefficient-filtration argument, using Stacks Tag 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian) and derived.tex Tag 0152

proof.text: Let $M\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ have cohomology in $[a,b]$. For every $r$, [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle], with its integer $n=-r$, gives the triangle $\mathcal H^r(M)[-r]\to\tau_{\ge r}M\to\tau_{\ge r+1}M\to\mathcal H^r(M)[-r+1]$. Apply $Rj_*$, which preserves triangles and shifts by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Each image of a cohomology sheaf is bounded constructible by Step 5. Starting at $\tau_{\ge b+1}M=0$ and descending through $r=b,\ldots,a$, closure under shifts and extensions in [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] proves that $Rj_*\tau_{\ge r}M$ is bounded constructible. Since $\tau_{\ge a}M\cong M$, this proves $Rj_*M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Only finitely many cohomology sheaves and filtration factors occur, so their individual bounds suffice.

source.place: Expose XIII, paragraph 1.1.2 (the derived-complex reformulation); Stacks perfect.tex Tag 08D4, proof of (2), for the successive lower-truncation triangles

proof.text:
Use [lem-exc-closed-ambient] for the ambient ordinary-etale right adjoint of closed direct image, and [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] for its natural distinguished triangle
$$i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow (i_*Ri^!K)[1].$$
This is the triangle in the ordinary module category for the finite ring $A=\Lambda$; no constructibility is assumed here. For bounded-below $K$, exact $j^*$ and the bounded-below right derived functor $Rj_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] make the middle and third terms bounded below. The category $D^+$ is triangulated [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], so the first term is bounded below too. Steps 1 and 2 give $Ri^!K\cong i^*i_*Ri^!K$ bounded below. Hence this adjoint restricts to $D^+$ and is the $i^!$ of the statement, by its right-adjoint property on this full subcategory.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic) and Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle); the cited closed-support triangle node states the arbitrary-complex finite-ring version

proof.text: Assume $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Step 1 gives $j^*K\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, and Step 6 gives $Rj_*j^*K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. In the localization triangle of Step 7, the middle and third terms are therefore bounded constructible. By [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory], rotating that triangle shows that $i_*i^!K$ is bounded constructible. The reflection assertion proved in Step 3 then gives $i^!K\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. This proves the forward implication.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.2, forward implication using XIII-1.1.1 and 1.1.2

proof.text: Conversely suppose that $j^*K$ and $i^!K$ are bounded constructible. Step 6 gives bounded constructibility of $Rj_*j^*K$, and Step 3 gives that of $i_*i^!K$. These are the third and first terms of the distinguished triangle in Step 7. Since [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] is a triangulated-subcategory assertion, it gives bounded constructibility of the middle term $K$. This proves the reverse implication and completes the equivalence.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.2, reverse implication using XIII-1.1.1 and 1.1.2

lean.statement: theorem isBoundedConstructible_iff_open_closed_exceptional (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) {X Z U : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (_hexc : ∀ V : X.affineOpens, IsExcellent Γ(X, V)) (_hinv : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (ℓ : X.presheaf.stalk x)) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (_hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (ℓ ^ n)))))) : DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (ℓ ^ n))) X K.obj ↔ DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (ℓ ^ n))) U ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (ℓ ^ n)))) j).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) ∧ DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (ℓ ^ n))) Z ((R(lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (ℓ ^ n)))) i)).rightAdjoint.obj K.obj)
